newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS puts CanOxy ratings under review.
newsitem.headline: DBRS puts CanOxy ratings under review.

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service said on Wednesday it placed the ratings of Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd's long-term unsecured debt and commercial paper under review with negative implications following CanOxy's bid for Wascana Energy Inc for about C$1.7 billion.

DBRS said CanOxy's cash offer to acquire all of the common shares of Wascana would result in a pro-forma annualized increase in CanOxy's barrel of oil equivalent production of about 42 percent and increase its proved barrel of oil equivalent reserves by close to 50 percent.
The bid is conditional on a two-thirds minimum acceptance rate.

DBRS said the deal could raise CanOxy's annualized cash flow by an estimated 20 to 25 percent, depending on energy prices. However, due to the significant premium over book value involved, there would be a sizable near-term negative impact on the combined earnings of the two companies due to incremental non-tax deductible amortization charges resulting from the revaluation of Wascana's assets.

Including debt assumed, net debt would rise by about C$2.0 billion to C$2.6 billion, representing close to 70 percent of capitalization, or about 2.5 times projected annualized cash flow, the bond rating service said.
It said no equity issues are currently contemplated.

DBRS said CanOxy's goal, if the offer is successful, would be to reduce the debt-to-cash flow ratio to 1.5 times within about two years. This would result in net debt representing close to 50 percent of capitalization, which is about peer group averages.
